title: FAIR IN MIND, FAIR IN ACTION? A SYNCHRONOUS BENCHMARK FOR UNDERSTANDING AND GENERATION IN UMLLMS

bias_targets.methodology: The paper evaluates gender bias by prompting models to generate images of various occupations and using a classifier (ARES) to measure the representation ratio of male vs. female figures. It also assesses understanding fairness by measuring accuracy disparities in identifying occupations for images of men vs. women, and tests the model's ability to generate counter-stereotypical gender examples.

The paper evaluates age bias by classifying generated images into young, middle-aged, and older categories to measure representation disparity across occupations. It also measures accuracy disparities in visual question answering tasks when identifying the occupations of people from different age groups.

The paper evaluates skin tone bias by classifying generated images into light, middle, and dark skin tones (using the Monk Skin Tone scale) to measure representation disparity. It also measures accuracy disparities and statistical parity differences in understanding tasks when processing images of people with different skin tones.

The paper evaluates intersectional bias by analyzing combinations of the three demographic attributes (Gender, Age, Skin Tone) simultaneously (e.g., 'young female light skin') to detect compounded biases in both image generation and visual understanding tasks.
